transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Laura (CTO, Verto), Diego (SRE), Rina (Head of Security), Jonah (Product), Priya (Compliance)

Summary (auto):
Quick follow-up after weekend degradation. Focus: short-term mitigations, telemetry gaps, long-term resilience changes to rollout and KV cache warming, and compliance notes around audit events and retention. Agree next steps and run bench.

Topics:
- Incident windows review (Mar 2 & Mar 5)
- KV cache cold start and warmup strategies
- Autoscale backpressure and pod churn effects
- Audit logs, token retention, and KMS/HSM discussion
- Safety pack + runbook handoff and bench scheduling

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone — thanks for joining, we know this was a bit disruptive, so we'll try to keep it practical. I'm Maya, I'll run the meeting. Ethan from our SE team is here. Verto folks, could we do quick intros?

[00:12] Laura (Verto CTO): Hi, Laura here. Thx. Long story short, we saw two short degradation windows last week, curious about what mitigation makes sense asap and how to avoid repeat.

[00:24] Diego (SRE): Yep, we had spikes for ~8-12 minutes on Mar 2 and Mar 5, p95 token time shot up and we saw throttles.

[00:34] Ethan (Redwood SE): Thanks, Diego. We pulled preliminary traces — looks like a mix of cold KV caches plus autoscaler scale-up lag. We wanted to talk through a tuning sweep and make sure the runbook covers safety fallbacks.

[01:15] Jonah (Product): Real quick — we have users timing out in app flows; Product wants clear SLOs for worst case.

[01:32] Maya: Understood. We'll map the SLOs to three levers: reduce cold starts (cache warmup), smoothing autoscale, and graceful fallthrough to smaller model or cached response.

[02:05] Rina (Security): Also we need to make sure audit events for these fallthroughs are recorded properly — compliance wants to know when requests hit fallback model or when KV cache misses spike.

[02:40] Ethan: Good point. Right now Redwood emits per-request metadata but it looks like Verto's retention policy trimmed some of those logs before you could correlate. Diego, can you confirm retention windows?

[02:58] Diego: We keep full request traces for 72 hours, aggregated metrics longer. Looks like the raw traces for Mar 2 were removed before we pulled them. That hurt root cause speed.

[03:15] Maya: Ok that's a telemetry gap. Short term, we recommend extending raw trace retention to 7 days for the trial period while we run the bench. We'll also push a sampling tweak so every suspected fallback gets full trace.

[03:45] Priya (Compliance): We need to check retention against our privacy policy; 7 days is fine if tokenized IDs are pseudonymized.

[04:02] Rina: Also KMS question — are audit logs safe to ship to our SIEM without exposing sensitive tokens?

[04:15] Ethan: Redwood can redact tokens and only surface request IDs and model variant tags. If you need HSM-backed key separation for encryption at rest, we can discuss Private deployment options.

[04:45] Laura: Are Private deployment/VMs necessary here? We're on Hosted now but are open if the SLA/regulatory impact is high.

[04:58] Maya: Let's hold that as a later decision. First we'll attempt operational mitigations in hosted: cache warmup, throttle shaping, and a controlled canary for fallback routing. If that doesn't resolve, we can propose Dedicated/Private.

[06:00] Ethan: For the Mar 2 window, a few details from traces: there was a surge of concurrent requests with long prompt prefixes. The runtime created a lot of KV cache entries causing memory pressure on a subset of pods — that raised GC and slowed token generation.

[06:28] Diego: Hmm, memory pressure on a subset — was that a single availability zone or spread?

[06:34] Ethan: Appeared to be spread but amplified where the cache warmup rate was higher. We saw poorer kernel selection (quantized vs fp16 paths) under memory pressure causing slower per-token times.

[06:55] Maya: We should flag fallback behavior: when a pod becomes overloaded Redwood can route to another pod or spin up a warm spare. The config we saw for Verto had relatively tight scale-up thresholds, so there was a window where requests queued.

[07:20] Jonah: So is the recommendation looser scale-up thresholds or pre-warmed standby instances?

[07:32] Ethan: Both: a modest increase to min replicas plus a short pre-warm pool for high-curie prompts. Also tuning the autoscaler cooldown from 120s to 60s for your traffic shape. But that increases cost — tradeoff.

[08:02] Diego: Cost is a concern. We need an approach that keeps costs near current budget but prevents the user impact.

[08:18] Maya: We can do a hybrid: pre-warm a small standby during business hours and rely on prefix caching to reduce per-request tokens for heavy prompts. Redwood Optimize will give quantization suggestions too.

[08:40] Rina: And we'd want clear indicators in the logs when requests hit standby/prefetch. That ties back to auditability.

[09:02] Ethan: We'll add a model_variant_tag and cache_hit boolean into structured logs for those requests and make them queryable in your SIEM.

[09:30] Laura: On the more immediate side, is there a fix we can flip within 24 hours?

[09:38] Maya: Short-term actions: extend trace retention to 7 days, enable verbose sampling for fallback events, and bump min replicas by 1 during peak windows. Those are quick changes.

[09:55] Diego: We can approve bumping min replicas during peak hours. Will need exact numbers.

[10:10] Ethan: We'll produce a proposed schedule with numbers based on your p95 traffic volume. I'll model cost delta.

[10:25] Maya: I'll follow up with the Safety Pack and runbook — that includes specific config toggles, dashboard queries, and rollback steps.

[11:00] Jonah: Can you walk through the KV cache warmup idea? Is this something we change in-app or in Redwood?

[11:12] Ethan: There are two parts: proactive warmup (issue synthetic prefixes to Redis-backed caches during predicted peaks) which you can orchestrate from app side or Redwood can do a lightweight prefetch; and in-runtime smarts that prioritize hot KV entries and evict cold ones more aggressively. For hosted you'll likely want Redwood to run prefetch for a small set of hot prompts.

[11:40] Laura: Prefetch as a managed feature sounds good. What are privacy implications?

[11:46] Priya: As long as prefetch doesn't log full prompt text. We need pseudonymization and only hashed keys.

[11:55] Ethan: Correct — we can only store and prefetch hashed prefix tokens; not the raw prompt. We'll document that.

[12:15] Diego: One oddity: on Mar 5 we saw a second window where p50 stayed okay but p95 degraded — suggests tail latency issues. Any ideas?

[12:28] Ethan: Tail latency often comes from stragglers — either noisy neighbor on host or slow kernel path due to a specific sequence length. We'll correlate host metrics and kernel path instrumentation.

[12:45] Maya: We'll also check if any model variant rollout occurred near that time — we saw some customers had automatic fallback to a quantized variant which can introduce different tail behaviors.

[13:05] Laura: We did a minor change in prompt routing on Mar 4. Could that affect Mar 5?

[13:12] Diego: We changed a routing rule to send long-context prompts to XL variant; might be related.

[13:25] Ethan: Ok that helps. We'll run controlled A/B bench to test whether the XL variant has worse p95 at your sequence lengths. We'll do sample runs with your traffic shape.

[13:55] Maya: On documentation and compliance: Rina and Priya, Redwood will provide a Safety Pack that includes the runbook, the list of log fields we will emit, and a privacy note about token redaction.

[14:15] Rina: We need assurance that audit logs have tamper-evident traces and time-aligned events for regulatory review.

[14:25] Ethan: We can include request hashes with time-synced event IDs and show mapping to model variant in exported events. For extra security we can surface signed audit archives if needed.

[14:40] Priya: Signed archives would be appreciated for quarterly compliance reviews.

[14:50] Maya: Noted. That's a possible add-on; we'll scope it separately.

[15:10] Diego: Back to ops — what's the recommended rollback if a model variant rollout causes tail instability?

[15:22] Ethan: We recommend immediate routing rollback to the previous stable variant and an automatic increase in pre-warmed replicas while the rollback completes. The runbook will include specific CLI/API commands.

[15:45] Jonah: How fast can that rollback happen? Seconds? Minutes?

[15:50] Ethan: Typically a few minutes to re-route traffic and spin up any necessary warm caches; depends on warm cache hit ratio. We'll document expected timelines (best effort 120–300s).

[16:15] Maya: Let's talk about the bench run. We propose a 1-hour controlled run during low-traffic window that replicates the Mar 2 traffic spike shape. We'll capture p50/p95, cache hit rates, and scale-up timelines.

[16:40] Laura: Good. When can we do that?

[16:45] Ethan: We can target Mar 15 as an initial slot; we need your sample traces to replay. Diego, can you provide those IDs and a sanitized traffic sample?

[16:56] Diego: I can. Note: sample contains PII in prompts — we'll sanitize before sending.

[17:05] Priya: We'll need a data handling agreement for generating synthetic traffic and any prompt material.

[17:12] Maya: We'll attach a short DPA addendum for bench traffic with agreed pseudonymization steps.

[17:28] Rina: One more question — you mentioned a fallback to a smaller model. How often should that be used before it's considered degraded UX?

[17:38] Ethan: That's a product tradeoff. We recommend a conservative threshold: fallback only when p95 crossing SLO for 3 consecutive windows of >5 minutes and after retries. We'll make this configurable.

[18:05] Jonah: Is there a way to show users a degraded mode message instead of silently returning smaller model results?

[18:14] Maya: Yes, we can surface a header or response flag so your frontend can show a ``Degraded mode'' banner. It's in the Safety Pack as a UX suggestion.

[18:35] Laura: Regarding cost — what's the incremental monthly if we increase pre-warmed replicas by 1 during business hours?

[18:43] Ethan: I'll send a cost delta table; rough estimate for your current usage is +6–9% depending on cloud spot availability. We'll model exact numbers in the follow-up.

[19:00] Diego: About the sampling change — if you increase verbose sampling for fallback events, does that increase trace storage significantly?

[19:12] Ethan: Small bump since fallback events are a small fraction; we'll sample at 100% only for fallback-tagged requests and otherwise keep current sampling.

[19:40] Priya: We need to ensure those traces are redacted before they cross our boundary into any external store.

[19:50] Ethan: Agreed — Redwood will redact prompt text prior to any external export. We'll provide the redaction rules.

[20:10] Maya: Quick organizational note: I'll be your AE point. Ethan will lead the bench and technical config. We'll do status sync after the bench.

[20:22] Maya: Now open floor — any other immediate concerns?

[20:30] Rina: One small ask: can Redwood provide an automated alert when cache miss rate exceeds X%? Ideally SNS/Slack.

[20:44] Ethan: Yes, we can add alert hooks. We'll propose thresholds based on baseline.

[21:05] Diego: Also, can we see per-pod memory histograms during the bench?

[21:12] Ethan: We'll push the extra host metrics to your Grafana for the run.

[21:30] Maya: Ok let's recap quickly — short term: extend trace retention to 7 days, enable fallback sampling, bump min replicas during peak, and add cache-miss alerts. Medium term: bench run Mar 15, runbook and Safety Pack delivery, signed audit archive option. Long term: consider Dedicated/Private if hosted mitigations don't meet SLOs.

[22:00] Laura: Sounds good. We'd like the runbook and Safety Pack by EOD 2027-03-09.

[22:10] Maya: We'll aim for that. Ethan, anything else?

[22:20] Ethan: I'll start the perf trace and modelling. Expect the trimmed perf trace and cost model by 2027-03-10.

[22:30] Diego: We'll get the sample IDs and sanitized traffic by 2027-03-09.

[22:45] Priya: And we'll review the DPA addendum; expect comments by 2027-03-10.

[23:00] Jonah: One last UX ask — can Redwood include the degraded response header example so front-end can implement quickly?

[23:06] Maya: Yes we'll include a sample header and client snippet in the Safety Pack.

[23:20] Rina: Thanks, this was productive.

[23:30] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts.

[23:45] -- End of meeting transcript --

Notes about transcription: occasional filler words and mis-hearings. Some proper nouns may be slightly altered (e.g., model variant names).
